 News | Brexit 
 UK PM Andy Burnham vows to renegotiate post-Brexit trade deal with EU
 UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham says renegotiating relationship with the EU could reverse some post-Brexit ‘damage’. 
 Listen (1 min) 
 Save
 Share UK PM Andy Burnham vows to renegotiate post-Brexit trade deal with EU on social media
 Share
 Add Al Jazeera on Google 
 Andy Burnham makes a statement in the House of Commons on Monday [AFP] 
 Published On 12 Oct 2026 12 Oct 2026 
 UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to push for closer relations with the European Union, confirming he will attend a bilateral summit in Brussels next month.
 Addressing parliament on Monday, Burnham said parts of the trade deal agreed with the EU after the UK voted to leave in 2016 would be renegotiated.
 Recommended Stories 
 list of 3 items list 1 of 3 The Burnham bounce: Is Labour gaining ground against Reform? 
 list 2 of 3 Burnham, Macron talk border security and stronger Europe-UK ties 
 list 3 of 3 UK PM Andy Burnham says it is ‘clear’ Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote 
 end of list Burnham said that the British public would be “the boss” at every stage of renegotiating Britain’s relationship with the EU and that he wanted “serious dialogue” about long-term ties.
 He told members of parliament that his focus at the summit would be boosting growth in the economy and controlling illegal immigration.
 Among the topics of discussion at November’s summit are cutting bureaucracy for British food exports and emissions trading, as well as a “new youth experience scheme” and deeper cooperation on immigration.
 The prime minister, who came into office in July, said the agreements could reverse some of the “damage” done to the post-Brexit British economy.
 He told MPs that Britain needed to “ take a calm, clear-eyed look at the world as it is today”.
 “Sticking to the status quo is not good enough,” he said, adding that “public opinion currently supports a pragmatic approach like the one I am suggesting”.
 After his address, the leader of the opposition, Kemi Badenoch , said Burnham would be unable to secure a better deal as the EU was ” tough negotiators” and warned that he had already “shown his hand”.
